{{nihongo|'''Tsukiyomi Shrine'''|月讀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iki Island]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are three: {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, Tsukuyumi-no-Mikoto, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. All three are the same deity.

The original deity was a “mountain deity,” but after Tachibana Mitsuyoshi’s identification, {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}} came to be regarded as the enshrined deity<ref name="#1"/>.

Tachibana Mitsuyoshi, who investigated Shikinaisha on {{ill|Iki Province|cs|Provincie Iki|de|Provinz Iki|es|Provincia de Iki|fa|ولایت ایکی|fr|Province d'Iki|id|Provinsi Iki|it|Iki (provincia)|ja|壱岐国|ko|이키국|lt|Ikio žemė|nl|Iki (provincie)|pt|Província de Iki|ru|Ики (провинция)|simple|Iki Province|sk|Iki (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ики|tr|Iki (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ікі|zh|壹岐國|zh_min_nan|Iki-kok|qid=Q1052938|lt=Iki Island}} by order of the {{ill|Hirado Domain|fa|قلمرو هیرادو|fr|Domaine de Hirado|ja|平戸藩|ko|히라도번|ru|Хирадо (княжество)|uk|Хірадо-хан|zh|平戶藩|qid=Q3034453}}, identified this shrine as “Tsukiyomi Shrine,” a Shikinaisha myōjin taisha. On June 1 of the same year, domain lord {{ill|Matsura Shigenobu|ja|松浦重信|zh|松浦重信|qid=Q11531889|lt=Matsura Shigenobu}} dedicated a stone shrine and one wooden mirror as {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}, and it was treated as a Shikinaisha for some time. Before that, however, it had no notable ritual facilities and was simply called “Yama no Kami” (mountain god). Mitsuyoshi had identified it as a Shikinaisha because the place was called “Kiyotsuki,” but it was also called “Fukatsuki,” whose origin is thought to be “fukafuchi”<ref>''Iki no Kuni Jinjaki''.</ref>. Therefore Mitsuyoshi’s judgment is considered mistaken, and the original Tsukiyomi Shrine is held to be {{ill|Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine|ja|箱崎八幡神社 (壱岐市)|qid=Q111442063|lt=Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine}}<ref name="#1"/>.

It is said that one of the “Tsukinobe stones” (moon-delay stones), which {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} is said to have placed against her abdomen during the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|ko|삼한 정벌|zh|三韩征伐|qid=Q11249435}} to delay childbirth, was dedicated here, but its whereabouts are now unknown.

At present, local residents including {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}} and worshippers from outside the island maintain and improve the shrine buildings and grounds.
